title: Wild inertia surjectivity and scaled tame characters in finite towers
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$ and residue characteristic $p>0$. Let $M/L/K$ be a tower with $M/K$ and $L/K$ finite Galois. For $X=L,M$, let $B_X$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $X$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_M$ of $B_M$ and put $\mathfrak n_L=\mathfrak n_M\cap B_L$. For each $X$, let $e_X=v_{(B_X)_{\mathfrak n_X}}(\pi_A)$ for a uniformizer $\pi_A$ of $A$, where the valuation of a uniformizer of $(B_X)_{\mathfrak n_X}$ is $1$. Let $D_X$ be the stabilizer of $\mathfrak n_X$ in $\operatorname{Gal}(X/K)$, let $I_X$ be its subgroup acting trivially on $\kappa(\mathfrak n_X)$, and let $\chi_X:I_X\to\mu_{e_X}(\kappa(\mathfrak n_X))$ be the uniformizer character and $P_X=\ker\chi_X$ of [lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia]. Write $e_X=q_Xn_X$ with $q_X$ a power of $p$ and $n_X$ prime to $p$, and set $\chi_{X,\mathrm{can}}=\chi_X^{q_X}:I_X\to\mu_{n_X}(\kappa(\mathfrak n_X))$. Restriction induces surjections $D_M\to D_L$, $I_M\to I_L$ and $P_M\to P_L$. One has $n_L\mid n_M$, and under the natural embedding of residue fields one has, for every $\sigma\in I_M$,
$$
\chi_{L,\mathrm{can}}(\sigma|_L)=\chi_{M,\mathrm{can}}(\sigma)^{n_M/n_L}.
$$
Each $\chi_{X,\mathrm{can}}$ is surjective and has kernel $P_X$, so the displayed power map is the transition on the tame quotient groups.

source.place: Tag 0BU7 (lemma-compare-inertia: surjective restriction on wild inertia, inertia and decomposition groups); Tag 0BU8 (remark-canonical-inertia-character: scaling by the p-part q and the n_M/n_L transition formula)

proof.text: First $\mathfrak n_L$ is maximal. Every element of $B_M$ is integral over $A\subseteq B_L$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], hence $S=B_M/\mathfrak n_M$ is integral over the embedded domain $R=B_L/\mathfrak n_L$. For $0\ne b\in R$, the element $b^{-1}$ of the field $S$ satisfies a monic equation over $R$; multiplying that equation by $b^{d-1}$, where $d$ is its degree, expresses $b^{-1}$ as an element of $R$. Thus $R$ is a field. This also explains the natural injection of residue fields used below.

source.place: Tag 0BU7, contracted maximal ideal setup; elementary monic-equation argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia] to $L/K$ and $M/K$ at these maximal ideals. Put $R_X=(B_X)_{\mathfrak n_X}$ and $k_X=\kappa(\mathfrak n_X)$. These are DVRs with fraction fields $X$. The lemma gives the uniformizer characters $\chi_X$, normal finite $p$-group kernels $P_X$, and surjections $\chi_X:I_X\twoheadrightarrow\mu_{n_X}(k_X)$, where $\mu_{n_X}(k_X)$ is cyclic of order $n_X$.

source.place: Tags 09E8 (remark-finite-separable-extension) and 09EE (lemma-galois-inertia), the input to Tag 0BU7

proof.text: The extension $M/L$ is finite Galois by the tower properties of normality and separability. If $b\in B_M$ is fixed by $\operatorname{Gal}(M/L)$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] gives $y\in L$ with image $b$. Integrality over $A$ descends along the injective field embedding $L\hookrightarrow M$, so $y\in B_L$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Thus $B_L\to B_M$ satisfies Mathlib's invariant-ring predicate for $\operatorname{Gal}(M/L)$. This permits the prime-conjugacy and quotient-residue-automorphism lifting clauses of [lem-exc-finite-galois-prime-residue-lifting] directly, without constructing fraction fields of the normalizations.

source.place: Tag 0BSX (lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois-compare), setup for applying Tag 0BRK over B_L

proof.text: For $\gamma\in D_L$, [lem-weil-pbc-normal-subextension-automorphism-extends] lifts $\gamma$ to $\tau\in\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)$. The primes $\tau(\mathfrak n_M)$ and $\mathfrak n_M$ of $B_M$ both contract to $\mathfrak n_L$, since $\gamma$ stabilizes $\mathfrak n_L$. Apply the prime-conjugacy clause of [lem-exc-finite-galois-prime-residue-lifting] using the invariant-ring structure of $B_L\to B_M$ for the finite Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(M/L)$ established in Step 3. It gives $\rho\in\operatorname{Gal}(M/L)$ with $\rho\tau(\mathfrak n_M)=\mathfrak n_M$. Thus $\sigma_0=\rho\tau\in D_M$ restricts to $\gamma$, proving decomposition surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0BSX, first half of its proof; Tag 0BU7, decomposition surjectivity input

proof.text: If $\gamma\in I_L$, construct $\sigma_0\in D_M$ as in Step 4. Its residue automorphism $\overline{\sigma_0}$ of $k_M$ fixes the embedded $k_L$, since its restriction is $\gamma$. The residue-lifting clause of [lem-exc-finite-galois-prime-residue-lifting], again with the invariant-ring structure of Step 3 and the quotient residue fields (the primes are maximal), gives $\eta\in\operatorname{Gal}(M/L)$ stabilizing $\mathfrak n_M$ and inducing $\overline{\sigma_0}$. Then $\eta^{-1}\sigma_0$ acts identically on $k_M$ and restricts to $\gamma$, so it belongs to $I_M$. Restriction preserves stabilizers by contraction and preserves trivial residue action by the injection $k_L\hookrightarrow k_M$. Thus both restriction maps are well-defined surjective homomorphisms, with the required $I_M\twoheadrightarrow I_L$.

source.place: Tag 0BSX, inertia case made explicit using the residue-automorphism lifting of Tag 0BRK; Tag 0BU7

proof.text: The inclusion $R_L\hookrightarrow R_M$ is local: an element of $B_L\setminus\mathfrak n_L$ stays outside $\mathfrak n_M$, while an element of $\mathfrak n_L$ maps into the maximal ideal of $R_M$. Choose uniformizers $t_L,t_M$. Using the discrete valuations in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], write $t_L=u t_M^r$ with $u\in R_M^\times$ and $r>0$. Writing $\pi_A=v t_L^{e_L}$ with $v\in R_L^\times$, whose image remains a unit, and taking $R_M$-valuations gives $e_M=r e_L$. Consequently $e_L\mid e_M$ and, on taking the prime-to-$p$ factors, $n_L\mid n_M$.

source.place: Tag 0BU7, uniformizer comparison; Tags 09E4 and 0BRL, definition and elementary multiplicativity of ramification indices

proof.text: For $\sigma\in I_M$, put $c=\sigma(t_M)/t_M\in R_M^\times$ and $b=(\sigma|_L)(t_L)/t_L\in R_L^\times$. Applying $\sigma$ to $t_L=u t_M^r$ yields $b=(\sigma(u)/u)c^r$. Since inertia acts trivially on $k_M$, the reduction of $\sigma(u)/u$ is $1$. Reduce this identity in $k_M$ and use the uniformizer formula of [lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia] to obtain $\chi_L(\sigma|_L)=\chi_M(\sigma)^r$, where $r=e_M/e_L$. In particular restriction sends $P_M$ into $P_L$.

source.place: Tag 0BU7, final paragraph and explicit b,c,unit calculation

proof.text: We spell out the wild-inertia lifting (the p-Sylow assertion of Tag 0BU7) without invoking a separate Sylow theorem. For $\gamma\in P_L$, choose $\tau\in I_M$ restricting to $\gamma$ using Step 5. By [lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia], $\chi_M(\tau)^{n_M}=1$, so $\tau^{n_M}\in P_M$. Since $P_L$ has $p$-power order, the order of $\gamma$ divides some $p^a$ (partition $P_L$ into cosets of the cyclic subgroup generated by $\gamma$). Choose a nonnegative integer $h$ with $hn_M\equiv1\pmod {p^a}$, possible because $n_M$ is prime to $p$. Then $\tau^{hn_M}\in P_M$ restricts to $\gamma^{hn_M}=\gamma$. Combined with Step 7 this proves $P_M\twoheadrightarrow P_L$.

source.place: Tag 0BU7, wild-inertia surjectivity paragraph; explicit elementary coprime-power lifting

proof.text: Raise the raw identity of Step 7 to the $q_L$-th power. As $e_M=r e_L$, $e_X=q_Xn_X$ and $n_L\mid n_M$, one has $r q_L=q_M(n_M/n_L)$. Hence $\chi_{L,\mathrm{can}}(\sigma|_L)=\chi_M(\sigma)^{r q_L}=\chi_{M,\mathrm{can}}(\sigma)^{n_M/n_L}$ in $k_M$. The equality with the left side shows that this power lies in the image of $\mu_{n_L}(k_L)$ under the residue-field embedding.

source.place: Tag 0BU8 (remark-canonical-inertia-character), scaled transition diagram and exponent identity

proof.text: Finally [lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia] says that $\chi_X$ is onto $\mu_{n_X}(k_X)$ with kernel $P_X$. Since $\gcd(q_X,n_X)=1$, choose $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ with $a q_X+b n_X=1$. For any $z\in\mu_{n_X}(k_X)$, $(z^{q_X})^a=z$, so raising to $q_X$ is an automorphism with inverse raising to $a$. Thus $\chi_{X,\mathrm{can}}=\chi_X^{q_X}$ has the same image and kernel. Identifying each tame quotient by this surjective character, Step 9 is exactly the induced power transition on those quotients. More explicitly, for $z\in\mu_{n_M}(k_M)$ choose $\sigma\in I_M$ with $\chi_{M,\mathrm{can}}(\sigma)=z$; Step 9 shows that $z^{n_M/n_L}$ lies in the embedded $\mu_{n_L}(k_L)$. Surjectivity of $I_M\to I_L$ and of $\chi_{L,\mathrm{can}}$ also shows that this power transition is onto.

source.place: Tag 0BU8, canonical-character isomorphism on the tame quotient; explicit Bezout inverse

proof_origin.place: Tags 0BU7 and 0BU8, with the restriction proof of Tag 0BSX written out using the finite prime-conjugacy and residue-lifting clauses of Tag 0BRK, and an explicit elementary coprime-power wild lift. In Lean the fixed-field theorem supplies the invariant-ring hypothesis directly; quotient residue fields suffice because both primes are maximal.
